thread:
maria: heads-up, getting a pile of p99 complaints for hosted text-generation in us-west-2 since ~08:45 UTC. Support triaged a customer incident (TKT-4729) and saw timeouts. p95 also creeping up.
ben: seeing it too on the dashboards. p99 spiked to ~1.2s for short prompts, and ~3.8s for long streams. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency
anita: customer says "requests hang then 504". I have the example request body and headers. Repro steps attached in the ticket.
leo: deploy-bot posted a rolling kernel upgrade in that cluster at 08:37. Could be related. @ben can you check node metrics?
ben: yep, checking now. node CPU fine, but GPU SM utilization super low on many nodes and NVLink errs on a couple. Also some RPC queue length spikes in the serving layer.
maria: could be a transient driver/kernel interop bug. We need a mitigation playbook for latency regressions: immediate throttles + fallback model + circuit breaker.
ben: agree. First quick mitigation: reduce per-tenant concurrency and enable circuit breaker to fail fast. I can push a global rate-limit at the ingress LB to cap QPS and reduce batching pressure.
anita: please do — customer TKT-4729 needs a temporary escalation mitigation.
leo: I'm going to disable the recent kernel rollout on the canary pool and redirect traffic away from canary nodes.
sre-oncall-bot: alert: p99_latency_us-west-2 > 1000ms for last 5m. incident_id=INC-2026-329
maria: mitigation plan (stepwise):
1) soft-rate-limit at LB (global) to 50r/s for public hosted endpoints in us-west-2 for 10m.
2) enable circuit-breaker in router to return 503 for queues > 200ms instead of piling up.
3) set fallback routing policy: route requests to "redwood-small-v1" in eu-west-1 for non-region-locked customers.
4) pause kernel rollout on canary nodes and cordon problematic nodes.
5) start a narrow canary rollback for serving runtime to the prior kernel.
6) monitor p95/p99 closely for 15m and then iterate.
ben: implementing LB rate limit now:

```
# kong/ingress rule
plugins:
  - name: rate-limiting
    config:
      second: 50
      policy: local
      limit_by: consumer
```
leo: cordoning nodes now: `kubectl cordon node-kernel-canary-{01..03}`
anita: I've told the customer we are applying temporary rate limits and asked for request IDs. They provided sample id `req_8a3f`.
ben: router config change: enabling circuit breaker threshold to 150ms queue time. snippet:

```
circuit_breaker:
  queue_time_threshold_ms: 150
  max_retries: 1
  fail_open: false
```
maria: add fallback model rule for non-geo-locked clients. config push to router with precedence.
ben: pushed the fallback rule: any request with header `X-Fallback-Allowed: true` will route to redwood-small-v1 in eu-west-1. For now we will set that header for non-enterprise tenants only.
anita: can we tag specific enterprise customers to be excluded? TKT-4729 is enterprise and must remain in-region.
leo: yes, we will keep enterprise in-region but reduce concurrency for them instead of fallback.
sre-oncall-bot: command: runbook apply mitigation-rate-limit-50-usw2 executed by ben at 08:52 UTC
maria: perf check: after LB + circuit breaker + cordon, p95 dropped from 420ms to 210ms in 6 minutes, p99 down to ~600ms. still above baseline but improving.
ben: NVLink errors persisted on two nodes so I've drained and rebooted them. That removed a source of RPC stalls.
leo: kernel rollback queued to canary pool. full rollback needs approvals but canary rollback to previous kernel image started.
anita: updating customer: told them temporary rate limit applied, fallback enabled for non-enterprise, we're doing kernel rollback and node remediation.
maria: a few follow-ups we need to do in the next 24h:
- add automated SLO guardrail that triggers a traffic cap and circuit-breaker when p99 > 800ms for 5m in a region.
- add an automated fallback policy that promotes a smaller quantized model in a secondary region when region latency breaches.
- add alert annotations linking to runbook steps and who to page.
ben: starting a PR for guardrail configs and docs. snippet of proposed PromQL alert for SLO guardrail:

```
record: region:p99_latency:5m
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{region="us-west-2"}[5m])) by (le))
alert: RegionP99High
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  runbook: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/latency-guardrails
```
leo: also propose a soft-circuit-breaker in the router that reduces batch sizes when queue_time > 50ms. reduces tail latency under pressure.
maria: good. also we should add tenant-level graceful-degradation: if backend signals overload, return structured hint `{"_fallback":true, "model":"redwood-small-v1"}` so SDKs can choose degrade UX.
anita: raising a support playbook entry so CS has canned responses.
ben: note for postmortem: root cause likely an interaction between kernel upgrade and NVLink driver that led to sporadic transport latency and queue buildup in the serving runtime; compounded by missing automated guardrail that would have capped load earlier.
maria: assign owners: ben -> immediate runtime config + PR, leo -> infra node remediation + rollback, anita -> customer comms + support playbook, me -> postmortem + SLO guardrail RFC.
anita: logged customer follow-up and will keep them updated. ticket TKT-4729 now marked "mitigation applied".
maria: monitoring: keep 1-min cadence for p95/p99 checks and we will reconvene in 30m. thanks all :rocket:
ben: leaving a debug command for repro:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_8a3f" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"short text"}'
```
leo: note: after node reboot and rollback, things are trending stable. still watching for residual NVLink oops.
sre-oncall-bot: resolved alert: p99_latency_us-west-2 returned to normal at 09:12 UTC. incident_id=INC-2026-329
maria: excellent. postmortem kickoff in #postmortems at 11:00 UTC. I'll drop the draft RFC for the SLO guardrail this afternoon.
anita: closing the customer loop now. will attach timeline and mitigation steps.
ben: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/834 (guardrail + circuit breaker defaults) — review ping @maria
maria: thanks — good coordination. we'll keep the playbook and runbooks updated based on lessons here. :white_check_mark:
